subject: general
question: Which group of crops belong to fibre crops and are produced on a large scale in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jute and hemp**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jute and hemp** are categorized as **fibre crops**.
 
• These crops are produced on a large scale in India due to the favorable climatic conditions.
 
• Fibre crops are primarily grown for their fibres, which are used in making ropes, bags, textiles, and other products.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of jute, which is often referred to as the '**Golden Fibre**'.
 
• Both jute and hemp have significant economic importance in the agricultural sector of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jute is mainly grown in the states of **West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam**.
 
• Hemp, although less common than jute, is also grown in different parts of India and has various industrial applications.
 
• These crops contribute significantly to rural employment and the economy.
 
• The cultivation of fibre crops like jute and hemp is encouraged by the government through various schemes and subsidies.
